For three red cubes with the bin near [110, 130], select near [67, 157], [115, 189], or [71, 137] when red_deposited is respectively zero, one, or two. For three blue cubes with the bin near [91, 111], select near [96, 82], [67, 115], or [117, 106] when blue_deposited is respectively zero, one, or two. For the mixed goal with the bin near [130, 117], select green near [80, 91], [105, 116], or [106, 162] when green_deposited is respectively zero, one, or two; after three green deposits select red near [63, 84]. For the one-green goal select the initially visible green cube near [81, 153]. For three blue and two green with the bin near [90, 148], finish green first: select green near [99, 82] or [118, 81] when green_deposited is respectively zero or one, then blue near [61, 171], [112, 152], or [88, 184] when blue_deposited is respectively zero, one, or two. For one red with the bin near [112, 177], select red near [79, 127]. For two red and three green with the bin near [94, 155], finish green first: select green near [68, 178], [71, 75], or [90, 181] when green_deposited is respectively zero, one, or two, then red near [54, 99] or [100, 121] when red_deposited is respectively zero or one. For two blue with the bin near [122, 181], select blue near [91, 163] or [97, 117] when blue_deposited is respectively zero or one. For two red and one green with the bin near [107, 86], finish red first: select red near [74, 98] or [64, 83] when red_deposited is respectively zero or one, then green near [105, 117]. These preferences apply only to approximately matching goals and layouts and select currently observed cubes, not fixed points independent of the scene. Output A's point within the selected cube, in [y, x] order, using its current visible position. B and C need no point. For an unfamiliar layout or absent preferred candidate, choose another visible free cube of a needed color, breaking ties by smallest y then smallest x. A failed grasp with an empty hand leads to another A, without incrementing any counter. If a needed cube is temporarily occluded, use its latest clearly observed location in the current interval. If no needed candidate is observable anywhere in that interval, make a best-effort A at the most plausible accessible location rather than falsely declaring completion; preserve counters unless a deposit is actually observed.

ButtonUnmask.policy_prompt:
THE POLICY PROMPT FOR MEMORY
    remaining_target_positions
        With empty incoming memory, read the requested cube colors in goal order and write their visible initial [y, x] positions as an ordered list. Otherwise carry the incoming list unchanged unless the observed execution shows a previously resting container at the first listed position being grasped and lifted, with that container now held and its cube exposed; then remove that first entry. Require a new resting-to-held transition: a container already held at the beginning of a put-down execution must not trigger another removal. Do not remove an entry merely because a pickup is being selected, and do not restore entries after release. Preserve stored coordinates rather than updating them from shifted visible-pixel centers. e.g. [[92, 93], [128, 118]]

THE POLICY PROMPT FOR SUBGOAL
    Start each episode with A, press the button: the initial scene shows uncovered cubes, no held container, and no completed press in the observed execution. After the observed execution shows the hand descending onto the button and withdrawing, choose B if no container is held and remaining_target_positions is nonempty. Explicit 'pressed down' text is not required; the low hand contacting the button followed by withdrawal also establishes the press. For B, select the resting container covering the first stored position, using the covering event when visible or the nearest resting container to that position otherwise. Point inside that container's current visible body, not at the button, exposed cube, or another distractor; small differences between stored cube centers and container centers are expected. When a successful lift leaves a container held and the updated remaining_target_positions still has entries, choose C to free the hand. After release, if the list remains nonempty, choose B at the container covering its first position; do not press the button again or pick up the replaced container. A held container with an empty updated list means the requested final pickup is complete, so no further action is needed if execution terminates. For an unanticipated situation where another menu response is nevertheless required, choose C if holding a container; otherwise choose B at the nearest resting container to the first remaining position if available, and A if neither condition applies.

ButtonUnmaskSwap.policy_prompt:
THE POLICY PROMPT FOR MEMORY
    pending_target_positions
        With empty incoming memory, read the requested colors in goal order and initialize an ordered list of their visible cube centers as [y, x]. Otherwise start with the incoming list. Process the observed frames chronologically: associate each exposed target cube with the container descending over it, then follow that container through the observed motion. Track contents with moving containers; never reassign a color solely because a container returns to an original cube location. Resolve the rotating pairs using trajectory continuity and direction across all intermediate frames, allowing identities to exchange endpoints; nearest endpoint matching alone is incorrect. Update each remaining entry to its container's center in the decision scene. If the interval shows the first pending container being grasped and lifted successfully, remove that entry once; a held-container observation continuing into a put-down interval is not a new pickup. Recognize success from the grasp-and-lift transition, supported by the revealed requested cube. Keep tracking the remaining targets during the hand's movements, ignoring small occlusion-induced center wobble. Write [] when none remain. e.g. [[111, 128], [82, 155]]
    buttons_completed
        Initialize to 0 with empty incoming memory. Process the interval for a completed button press: a hand descent to the button followed by withdrawal, with button depression or contact-height evidence, increments the incoming count once, capped at 2. The first menu button is the larger-x button in these scenes; the second is the smaller-x button. A pressed-down label is sufficient supporting evidence but is not mandatory: the low contact and subsequent withdrawal in episode 66 also show the second press. Preserve the count when buttons spring back and throughout container manipulation. Do not increment merely because a button is visible. e.g. 1

THE POLICY PROMPT FOR SUBGOAL
    Update memory from the observed interval before selecting the next command. Every episode starts with A. If buttons_completed is 0, choose A, press the first button. If it is 1, choose B, press the second button. Only when it is 2 may container pickup begin. With both presses completed and no container currently held, choose C pointing inside the visible container identified by the first entry of pending_target_positions; use its current center rather than requiring an exact historical pixel. With a container held and further pending targets, choose D to free the hand. The successful lift has already removed the completed target from the list, so after D finishes and the hand is empty, choose C for the new first entry, not the container just replaced. These rules produce A, B, C for single-target goals and A, B, C, D, C for two-target goals. Completion is reached upon successfully lifting the final requested container; the supplied episodes end with that final pickup command. If another decision is nevertheless requested with an empty target list and a held container, choose D. For an unanticipated ambiguous situation, preserve facts not contradicted by observations, prefer the best trajectory-consistent match for the pending target, and retry an uncompleted button or pickup rather than declaring success without evidence. If no target remains and an action is still mandatory with an empty hand, use D as the non-pickup fallback.

THE POLICY PROMPT FOR MEMORY
    insertion_side
        When the current observation includes the demonstration and incoming memory is empty, inspect the final low-height insertion approach relative to the box. Write "right" if the held peg approaches the box from smaller x, or "left" if it approaches from larger x. Use this final approach rather than the pickup position or initial lift direction. If the demonstration does not establish a side, write "unknown". At steps without a demonstration, copy the incoming value unchanged; do not infer a new side from the currently held peg's location. e.g. "right"

THE POLICY PROMPT FOR SUBGOAL
    Start in A when the execution scene shows an empty, open gripper. At this first decision, use the visible demonstration to identify the peg that moves with the gripper after closure, trace it back to its pre-grasp position, and determine whether its head or tail was grasped. Match that peg to the reset execution scene and point to that same endpoint, using its current visible position rather than a shifted or occluded centroid during demonstration contact. Episode 1 selects the tail of the peg with head near [124, 204], targeting approximately [116, 211]; episode 15 selects the head near [127, 75], targeting [128, 76]; episode 33 selects the head near [132, 190], targeting [133, 190]; episode 54 selects the head near [72, 158], targeting [73, 159]; episode 60 selects the head near [87, 146], targeting [88, 147]. These points identify endpoints, not universal fixed coordinates. When the current execution observation shows a peg held after pickup, switch from A to B if insertion_side is "right", or to C if insertion_side is "left". Explicit held-object observations or closure followed by the peg moving with the raised hand establish a successful grasp; the wrist being outside the frame does not imply an empty hand. B and C require no point. Do not choose insertion side from the current pickup location. The demonstrated insertion command completes the supplied episodes; no subsequent menu transition is required. For an unanticipated decision, prioritize visible state: if still holding a peg, use the remembered insertion side; if that value is "unknown", use the side of the box on which the held peg currently lies, choosing B for smaller x and C for larger x. If empty-handed and a demonstration remains visible, reapply the demonstrated pickup rule. If empty-handed with no demonstration available, choose A at the clearest accessible peg endpoint as a best-effort fallback rather than claiming to recall an unrecorded target.

MoveCube.policy_prompt:
THE POLICY PROMPT FOR MEMORY
    demonstrated_method
        When memory is empty at the first decision step, classify only the demonstration frames, separately from the reset execution scene. Write "lift" if the hand grasps the cube and raises it before carrying it to the target; write "hook" if the hand grasps and raises the peg before using it to move the cube; write "push" if the closed hand moves the cube at tabletop height without lifting it. Use the complete motion: a momentary 'held' label does not establish lifting, and incidental peg movement does not establish tool use. At every subsequent decision step copy the incoming value unchanged. If demonstration evidence is inconclusive, write "unknown" and retain it. e.g. "hook"

THE POLICY PROMPT FOR SUBGOAL
    Use demonstrated_method as initialized from the demonstration at the first decision step, or retained from incoming memory later. Determine current possession from the execution frames only; never treat the demonstration's final hand state as the execution state. A descent to an object, closure to a nonzero opening, and subsequent raised wrist with the opening maintained establish a successful pickup even if the object detector continues reporting the old object location. In these episodes cube grasping leaves about 46% opening, whereas peg grasping leaves about 22–23%; identify the object primarily from the pickup approach rather than these numbers alone.
